assumptions_held: The business-quality and valuation judgements were correct. Reverse DCF implied the market demanded 8.6pct FCF growth from a company delivering 32pct; switching costs in CAD/PLM were correctly identified as punitive. That gap is exactly what attracted a strategic acquirer.
assumptions_broken: My explicit claim that upside was STRUCTURALLY CAPPED. I wrote: a 9pct grower does not re-rate dramatically, reaching plus-20pct needs multiple expansion which I cannot point to a reason for. Target 152 (plus 18pct). Actual outcome: acquired at 205 cash (plus 59pct). I scored catalysts 5/10 for having no dated event, and treated absence of a visible catalyst as absence of upside.
reviewer_notes: RESOLVED BY ACQUISITION. Schneider Electric definitive agreement 2026-10-05 at 205 USD/share cash, approx 23.7B, board approved, expected close Q3 2027. Now trading 194.39, a 5.2pct spread to the offer. The original thesis is COMPLETE - remaining upside is merger arbitrage over roughly 9 months, not the business thesis I underwrote.

assumptions_held: The structural AI-intermediation risk I flagged in the thesis - something inserting itself between traveller and OTA - is materialising: Meta launched its Muse AI agent and Expedia integrated it. I named the shape of this risk correctly, though I named Google rather than Meta.
assumptions_broken: My BASE case assumed the company delivers its guided high-single-digit growth. Guidance was CUT and new debt raised.
